steps.title: 1.1 Run the print queue
steps.text: Print the 12 parts in the order of the print queue table below. Two can start now (rudder blade, bow cone). Each plate: clear the bed, start the next file, pull the part when cool, peel the brim.

meta.tools: P1S, PETG (4.5 kg needed; you own 4: buy 1 more spool)
meta.wait: see the print queue: 5 of 12 prints wait on a measurement

steps.title: 1.2 Press in the threaded inserts
steps.text: Soldering iron with an insert tip: 2 x M5 into the root cap's bar seat, 2 x M4 into the rudder housing for the cover.

meta.tools: soldering iron + insert tip, M5 and M4 heat-set inserts

steps.title: 2.1 Cut the pipe
steps.text: Mark 1594 mm with a paper wrap so the cut is square, cut, file the burr off both ends inside and out.

meta.tools: saw (hand or circular), paper wrap, file, tape measure

steps.title: 2.2 Measure the pipe inside diameter, order the plugs
steps.text: Calipers, 4 readings at each end (the plugs grip the inside). Send the numbers to the designer; the designer checks them against the Cherne 270288 grip range and you order 2.

steps.title: 2.3 Paint the outside of the pipe
steps.text: Scuff with 220 paper, wipe, 2 coats. Mask the bands where the saddle, fin mount, housing and panels get bonded (glue holds to bare scuffed PVC, not to paint).

meta.tools: 220 sandpaper, masking tape, roller or rattle can

steps.title: 2.4 Drill the 2 cable holes
steps.text: Hole 1 under the mast socket (solar panel + sail-sensor cables), hole 2 under the rudder housing (servo cable). Positions from the model; potted later (steps 5.5 and 6.3).

steps.title: 3.1 Measure the plate, print the fin mount
steps.text: Calipers at 6 points on the steel plate. the designer sets the slot to the thickest reading + 0.3 mm and re-exports the two fin mount halves; print both (24 h of printing).

meta.wait: plate delivery (~8 days after the upload) + thickness reading

steps.title: 3.2 Glue the fin mount to the pipe bottom
steps.text: Wrap the plate in release tape and slide both halves onto it: the plate is the jig that lines them up. Glue the halves to the pipe bottom, strap, check the plate hangs straight down with a level. Pull the plate after the glue sets.

meta.tools: structural epoxy, release tape, 2 ratchet straps, level

steps.title: 3.3 Fit the fin pin
steps.text: Slide the plate in, push the 10 mm ball-lock pin through the mount and the plate's hole, tie the lanyard to the mount.

steps.title: 4.1 Cut the mast and the sleeve
steps.text: Mast tube to 1960 mm, PVC sleeve to length from the parts table. File both ends.

steps.title: 4.2 Glue the mast socket on
steps.text: Glue the sleeve into the saddle and the stop collar onto the sleeve (stops 35 degrees each side of straight ahead). Glue the saddle on the pipe top at 602 mm from the bow end, square to the pipe.

steps.title: 4.3 Drill the mast pin hole
steps.text: With the mast in the socket, drill one 1/4 in hole through saddle, sleeve and mast at 140 mm above the pipe centre. Push the ball-lock pin through; tie its lanyard.

steps.title: 4.4 Build the wing (fold, not carve)
steps.text: (1) Check the flutes run along the 8 ft length; tape the 1:1 pattern on, cut the outline and the root notch with a knife against a straightedge. (2) Clamp a 1/2 in dowel on the nose line, warm 300 mm at a time with a heat gun on low, roll the sheet round the dowel until the halves meet at the back, hold till cool; slide the dowel out. (3) Cut the 5 coroplast ribs from the leftover, 33 mm mast hole at 15% chord each; trim the front 158 mm off the root rib. (4) Slide the ribs to their marks (1/4, 1/2, 3/4 span + root + tip), hot-glue to locate. (5) Close the back edge: 25 mm flap inside, clamp, drill + pop-rivet every 75 mm with backing washers. (6) Root cap (magnet already in its tab) into the root front, 4 x M4 screws through both skins into its inserts; tip bushing in the tip rib. Slide the wing down the mast onto the root bushing: it should swing freely between the two stops. No glue on the polypropylene is load-bearing.

meta.tools: straightedge, knife, 1/2 in dowel, heat gun, clamps, drill, pop-rivet tool, hot-glue gun, soldering iron (inserts)

steps.title: 4.5 Make and fit the counterweight bar
steps.text: Cut the steel flat to 256 mm, drill 2 holes, fit the 2 thumbscrews into the root cap. Balance check: with the boat level the wing should stay wherever you leave it (no swing to either side).

steps.title: 4.6 Masthead cap: camera + radar reflector
steps.text: Pot the camera behind the window disc in the cap, push the reflector onto the cap's spigot, cap onto the mast top.

meta.wait: camera in hand (cap print waits on its size)

steps.title: 5.1 Gel test on a scrap of servo cable
steps.text: Gel a cut-off piece of the servo cable, let it cure, leave it under water 24 h, then peel it. Pass = dry inside + peels clean.

meta.tools: the gel, a cup of water

steps.title: 5.2 Read the servo spline
steps.text: Count the teeth on the horn that ships with the servo (expected 15). Send the count and the case size to the designer; then print the housing and cover.

steps.title: 5.3 Make the rudder post
steps.text: Cut the 3/4 in aluminium rod, drill the 2 cross holes (1/4 in) and the 2 dowel holes that match the horn, press the dowels in.

meta.tools: hacksaw, drill press, 1/4 in bit, dowel bit
meta.wait: servo in hand (dowel spacing = horn holes)

steps.title: 5.4 Soft-pot the servo
steps.text: Gel over the case seams and the cable entry, same way as the test piece.

steps.title: 5.5 Glue the rudder housing on, pot cable hole 2
steps.text: Glue the housing to the pipe bottom at the stern, run the servo cable through hole 2, fill the hole with potting epoxy.

steps.title: 5.6 Put the rudder together
steps.text: Post up through the blade and the housing bore, blade pin, post-up pin. Horn onto the servo spline and onto the dowels, servo slides in from aft, cover on with 2 M4 screws.

steps.title: 6.1 Check the battery
steps.text: Unbox the WattCycle 12.8 V 20 Ah LiFePO4 (protection board built in); check 13.0-13.4 V at its Mini-Fit pigtail.

steps.title: 6.2 Lay out the electronics row
steps.text: Our main board on its 4 standoffs, the GPS puck, RockBLOCK 9603, SPOT Trace, Genasun GV-5 and a humidity card on the row inside the pipe, then the 10 plug cables, each into its own keyed plug (no hand wiring); the battery goes LAST (aft end): that is what keeps the boat level.

meta.wait: board parts delivery; tracker takes 11-18 days

steps.title: 6.3 Solar panels on, pot cable hole 1
steps.text: Glue the 4 panels on the pipe top (3 mm gaps), run their cables and the TMAG5273 cable through hole 1, fill the hole with potting epoxy.

steps.title: 6.4 Bench power-up
steps.text: Sun on the panels: battery charges. GPS gets a fix. One satellite message goes out. Backup tracker pings. Servo sweeps the rudder end to end.

steps.title: 6.5 Close the hull
steps.text: Plugs into both ends, tighten. Cones on, one worm clamp each.

steps.title: 7.1 Leak check
steps.text: Pull the hull down to -5 inHg and watch the gauge 30 min (loss 0.3 or less), then tie it off at the dock 24 h. Open the stern plug: humidity card still blue.

meta.tools: hand vacuum pump + gauge, dock line

steps.title: 7.2 Compass turn-through
steps.text: On level ground away from steel and cars, turn the boat slowly through 2 full circles while the main board logs.

steps.title: 7.3 Wing-magnet table
steps.text: Move the wing stop to stop; the board logs the sensor at 0, 17 and 35 degrees each side.

steps.title: 8.1 Load the Jetta
steps.text: Fin out (pull the pin), rig out (pull the mast pin, lift mast + wing), cones off. The rudder stays on. Hull goes in through the folded seat.

steps.title: 8.2 First float at the ramp
steps.text: Put it back together (fin + pin, cones + clamps, mast + pin, counterweight bar) and float it on a line. Check: pipe top above water about 64 mm at the bow, 78 mid, 92 stern; sits level; push the mast tip to the water and let go: it comes back up.

steps.title: Car trip: 1. Pull the mast pin
steps.text: Pull the ball-lock pin out of the saddle; it stays on its lanyard.

steps.title: Car trip: 2. Lift the mast + wing out
steps.text: Lift mast, wing and masthead straight up out of the sleeve; unplug the camera at the M8 plug in the bore.

steps.title: Car trip: 3. Pull the fin pin
steps.text: Pull the 10 mm ball-lock pin through the fin mount.

steps.title: Car trip: 4. Fin plate down and out
steps.text: Slide the steel plate straight down out of the mount.

steps.title: Car trip: 5. Blade bolt out
steps.text: Undo the nyloc, push the 1/4-20 bolt out.

steps.title: Car trip: 6. Blade off
steps.text: Slide the blade down off the post.

steps.title: Car trip: 7. Ready for the Jetta
steps.text: Pipe, mast + wing, fin plate and blade travel as 4 pieces.

steps.title: 15-minute dock swap: 1. Stern cone off
steps.text: Loosen the thumb-screw clamp, pull the cone.

steps.title: 15-minute dock swap: 2. Stern plug out
steps.text: Loosen the Cherne plug, pull it.

steps.title: 15-minute dock swap: 3. Tray out by the plugs
steps.text: Unplug every cable at its plug, slide the tray out the stern end.

steps.title: 15-minute dock swap: 4. Swap the battery
steps.text: Straps off, lift the battery out, drop the fresh one in, straps on.

steps.title: 15-minute dock swap: 6. Tray back in, plug up
steps.text: Slide the tray in, plug every cable back.

steps.title: 15-minute dock swap: 7. Plug and cone back
steps.text: Seat the plug, tighten it; cone on, clamp tight.
